# MCP Servers

> Connect Empryo to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers over stdio, HTTP or SSE, so the agent can use their tools next to the built-in ones.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for giving AI agents extra tools. Connect an MCP server to Empryo and the agent can call its tools, for example to open GitHub issues or query Sentry, alongside its built-in tools.

Use it when the agent needs a service Empryo does not cover out of the box.

## Quick start

Add a server to `mcpServers` in your config. This one runs the GitHub server as a local process:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": [
    {
      "name": "github",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"],
      "env": { "GITHUB_TOKEN": "ghp_..." }
    }
  ]
}
```

Restart Empryo or open `/mcp` to check it connected. The server's tools are now available to the agent as `mcp__github__<tool>`.

If you copy a config from another tool that writes `mcpServers` as an object keyed by server name, that works too. Empryo reads the key as the server's `name`.

## Where the config lives

- **Global:** `~/.empryo/config.json` applies to every project.
- **Project:** `.empryo/config.json` applies to one repository. A project server with the same `name` as a global one replaces it.

A project's MCP servers start only after you trust the repository with `/trust`. This stops a cloned repo from running commands on your machine without your say.

## Three ways to connect

| Transport | Use it for | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `stdio` (default) | A server that runs as a local program | `command`, optional `args`, `env`, `cwd` |
| `http` | A remote server over Streamable HTTP. Use this for new remote servers | `url`, optional `headers` |
| `sse` | Older remote servers that only speak Server-Sent Events | `url`, optional `headers` |

```json
{
  "mcpServers": [
    {
      "name": "sentry",
      "transport": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/sse",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ..." }
    },
    {
      "name": "legacy-service",
      "transport": "sse",
      "url": "https://legacy.example.com/events",
      "disabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Settings

| Field | Type | What it does |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `name` | string (required) | The server's name. Also the prefix of its tool names |
| `transport` | `"stdio"` \| `"http"` \| `"sse"` | How to connect. Default `"stdio"` |
| `command` | string | Program to start (stdio) |
| `args` | string[] | Arguments for `command` |
| `env` | `Record<string,string>` | Environment variables for the program |
| `cwd` | string | Working directory for the program (stdio) |
| `url` | string | Server address (http, sse) |
| `headers` | `Record<string,string>` | HTTP headers, such as `Authorization` (http, sse) |
| `timeout` | number | Time limit for each tool call, in ms. Default 30000 |
| `disabled` | boolean | Keep the entry but don't connect |
| `resident` | boolean | Always send this server's tools to the model instead of loading them on demand. Use it for a server you rely on every turn. The set is fixed when a session starts, so the prompt cache holds: a server pinned later, or one that was not connected at startup, is reached on demand until the next session, and a pinned server that disconnects keeps its tools, which answer that it is not connected |
| `redirect` | `"follow"` \| `"error"` | Whether a remote server may redirect. Set `"follow"` only if the server needs it |

## Tool names

Every MCP tool is renamed to `mcp__<server>__<tool>` so it can never clash with a built-in tool. A server named `github` with a tool `create_issue` gives the agent `mcp__github__create_issue`.

## Connection behavior

- All enabled servers connect when Empryo starts, up to four at a time.
- If a local (stdio) server crashes, Empryo restarts it, up to three times with a growing delay.
- A remote server that fails stays failed until you retry it from `/mcp`.
- When Empryo exits, it closes every connection and stops every local server.

## Manage servers in the terminal UI

Run `/mcp` to see each server's status and tools.

| Key | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Type | Filter servers by name |
| `Ctrl+A` | Add a server |
| `Ctrl+E` | Edit the selected server |
| `Ctrl+D` | Delete the selected server |
| `Ctrl+T` | Turn the selected server on or off |
| `Ctrl+R` | Reconnect a failed server |
| `Ctrl+P` | Ping a connected server |
| `Tab` | Switch to the tools list |
| `Enter` | Open the server's details |

## Headless runs

MCP servers also connect in headless mode, so scripts and CI jobs can use them:

```bash
empryo --headless "use the github MCP to list open issues"
```

"""Replay saved effort predictions; CPU only, no inference and no private text output."""
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np

base = Path('/mnt/zer0models/z0-wt/salvage/sft-round2/turn-effort-router')
private = Path.home() / '.z0int/research/sft-round2/turn-effort-router'
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('empryo_effort_audit_scorer', base / 'score.py')
score = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(score)
evaluation = score.load(private / 'data/eval.jsonl')
train = score.load(private / 'data/train.jsonl')
truth = np.array([score.gold(row) for row in evaluation])
train_sessions = {row['meta']['session'] for row in train}
eval_sessions = {row['meta']['session'] for row in evaluation}
def input_digest(row):
    return hashlib.sha256(row['messages'][1]['content'].encode()).digest()
input_overlap = len({input_digest(row) for row in train} & {input_digest(row) for row in evaluation})
reports = []
for path in (private / 'preds').glob('*.jsonl'):
    if 'q06b_e2' not in path.name or 'constrained' not in path.name:
        continue
    predictions = {row['id']: row for row in score.load(path)}
    matched = sum(row['id'] in predictions for row in evaluation)
    if matched != len(evaluation):
        reports.append({'candidate': 'q06b_e2_constrained', 'matched': matched, 'verdict': 'INCOMPLETE_MATCH'})
        continue
    predicted = np.array([score.BI.get(score.parse_pred(predictions[row['id']]), -1) for row in evaluation])
    baselines = score.baseline_preds(train, evaluation)
    indexes = score.boot_idx([row['meta']['session'] for row in evaluation], nboot=2000, seed=0)
    model_boot = [score.macro_f1(truth[index], predicted[index]) for index in indexes]
    differences = {}
    for name in ['metadata_prior', 'naive_bayes_ref']:
        difference = [value - score.macro_f1(truth[index], baselines[name][index]) for value, index in zip(model_boot, indexes)]
        differences[name] = {'macro_f1_difference': score.macro_f1(truth, predicted) - score.macro_f1(truth, baselines[name]), 'paired_session_bootstrap95': score.ci(difference)}
    metrics = score.metrics(truth, predicted)
    reports.append({'candidate': 'q06b_e2_constrained', 'matched': matched, 'eval_n': len(evaluation), 'metrics': metrics, 'session_bootstrap95': score.ci(model_boot), 'comparisons': differences, 'passes_required_recall_gate': metrics['recall_41plus'] >= 0.5})
print(json.dumps({'inference_calls': 0, 'bootstrap_samples': 2000, 'bootstrap_seed': 0, 'train_rows': len(train), 'eval_rows': len(evaluation), 'eval_sessions': len(eval_sessions), 'session_overlap': len(train_sessions & eval_sessions), 'exact_input_overlap': input_overlap, 'reports': reports}, indent=2))

# z0intelligence history audit

## Scope and confidence

This audit separates committed source, branch-only implementations, local experiments, historical reports and running processes. It inventories all 77 issues across z0intelligence and z0, and 97 z0intelligence PRs. That is not a claim to have independently verified every issue or PR implementation. Deeper source tracing covered memory, shadow decisions, episode preparation and training. No new inference, training, GPU work, service restart, GitHub write or production source edit was performed in this audit.

My previous advice was premature: I had not reconciled branch-only SFT interfaces with the separate local research trainers. Reading a trainer script or a round-numbered directory does not prove a run; accepting a remembered claim of zero runs also does not replace inspection.

## History reconstructed

- September 16–18: OpenJev decision readouts, trainable scorer tooling, next-action/ridge research, onboarding, receipts and execution-versus-verified-outcome separation.
- September 26–30: canonical cognition, decision backends, resident bridge, routing/dispatch authority and mechanism-neutral architecture. `src/z0int/train.py` is a time-split ridge baseline, not an instruction-model SFT trainer.
- October 2: #109 reconciled downstream components including EventLog, OptMem and scoped memory contracts; #110 documents the squash integration. Several original PRs are closed without their own merge event because their content was integrated through reconciliation. Closed-unmerged is therefore not sufficient evidence that code was discarded.
- October 3 wiring remains a separate lineage: `integrate/wiring-20261003` contains memory surface/seam, capture and loop export absent from audited origin/master. It is 96 commits ahead and seven behind that pinned mainline, not an installation-ready small patch.
- October 5–11: OptChat, FFF retrieval and selected salvage fixes landed. Origin/master is `dd39238`; live master is `4de1aa9`, diverged by three local versus five remote commits, with additional uncommitted changes. Neither committed ref alone describes the live working tree.
- October 14 episode/SFT branches contain `episodes.py`, `episode_split.py`, `episode_eval.py`, `episodes_cli.py` and `sft_adapter.py`. `origin/feat/sft-routing-slice-v0` contains current origin/master plus 113 commits. These are not absent just because they are missing from master.

## Training: the distinction I missed

The branch's repository SFT adapter defaults to a stub. `UnslothLoRABackend.train()` explicitly raises `NotImplementedError` after availability checking; remote Tinker training is disabled. That repository interface does not establish an executed training loop.

Separately, the local round-2 research area now contains 19 adapter weight files with nonzero sampled LoRA-B tensors and 17 logs containing training-completion metrics after stripping ANSI formatting. Artifact dates include October 15–16. These are evidence of local training activity; they must not be counted as 19 distinct successful experiments because checkpoints, repeated attempts and copied outputs require lineage reconciliation. They also do not establish production deployment or verified benefit. I did not establish when each run occurred relative to Kevin's earlier correction that no SFT runs had been done.

There is stronger evidence for one specific offline result:

- `sft-round2/turn-effort-router/TRAIN.md` records QLoRA runs and points to private adapters/predictions.
- The current dataset has 5,578 train and 1,040 evaluation rows; evaluation spans 187 sessions and 1,040 near-duplicate clusters.
- I recomputed the saved `q06b_e2` constrained predictions against all 1,040 matching evaluation IDs, with no inference. Macro-F1 **0.471689**, accuracy **0.475**, recall for the `41+` bucket **0.461240**, parse-failure rate **0**.
- I independently recomputed the same simple baselines: naive Bayes macro-F1 **0.369256**, metadata prior **0.331919**, length rule **0.299073**, keyword rule **0.280971**.
- This reproduces the saved aggregate report, but the candidate still fails its required `recall(41+) >= 0.50` gate. The saved confidence intervals were inspected, not independently recomputed in this audit. Current scorer code distinguishes session bootstrap from the earlier per-near-duplicate-cluster bootstrap; 1,040 distinct clusters do not imply 1,040 independent sessions.
- Predicting observed tool-call effort is not demonstrating that a cheap model can replace the frontier agent. The dataset card explicitly treats this router as advisory.

Thus the previous blanket statements “no SFT has run” and “no model has beaten a simple baseline” are not safe descriptions of the currently observed local artifacts. A supported narrower statement is: one offline effort-router result reproduces above its simple baselines, but fails its stated acceptance gate; end-to-end verified savings remain unestablished.

## Runtime and ownership

Passive process inspection found intelligence-service processes rooted in the live checkout and no process matching the cognition-supervisor module. That is not a complete endpoint health test and does not identify the exact source already loaded by a resident process. I did not restart or probe inference services.

The existing serving-race repair remains on its own one-commit branch and was not modified. Codex's PR #150 and z0evals #95 were left alone. Cross-repo ownership still separates evidence/state/runtime in z0intelligence, experimentation in Evolution Lab, independent evaluation in z0evals and canonical identity in z0. Existing extraction-library integration was not independently exercised in this audit.

## Remaining uncertainty and next decision

High confidence: the pinned source boundaries, main-versus-branch file presence, stub-versus-external-training distinction and recomputed effort-router point metrics. Lower confidence: complete per-run lineage across all round-2 tasks, the deployment state, causal benefit and which optimization should be promoted.

Next work should reconcile existing run manifests, reproduce their acceptance gates with session-aware uncertainty and inspect the newest round-2 outputs before recommending either new training or a new data/eval platform. The earlier parser patch remains a separate bounded correctness fix, not evidence that the learning pipeline works.

## Empryo workspace correction

Creating a worktree with shell git commands did not move this tab's project engine: its Genome and project memory still belonged to the live checkout. The documentation says project memory writes `.empryo/memory.db`, and that database exists in the live checkout; my earlier project-memory writes were therefore in the wrong project context. My earlier “live checkout untouched” wording was too broad: no production source was edited, but I used project memory there. This tab is scheduled to move through Empryo's worktree tool to `empryo/shadow-measurement` after this turn, so the next message gets the matching engine and Genome. No existing memory database was deleted or rewritten as part of this audit.

Documentation checked: https://empryo.com/docs/surfaces/desktop#worktrees and https://empryo.com/docs/tools/memory . Empryo memory is not automatically the z0 EventLog or a verified training history.
